title: Wipe as a verified, redundant, BHK-first transaction: regenerate the page-126 BHK before touching the SEs, Hamming-distant double-checked wipe verdicts, and a boot-time 'wipe verified' assertion that keeps the armed flag until every region and both SEs are confirmed gone
threat: A wipe (10 wrong PINs, tamper, admin) that is interrupted, glitched or partially executed leaves recoverable state: the SE050 half remains readable under still-valid SCP03 keys, the OPTIGA half survives a failed factory_reset, a single-bool verdict is coerced to 'wiped' (SE17-3), and the next boot has no obligation to finish. Today the page-125 flag covers only the SE050 admin object.
proposal: (1) Make the first irreversible step of every wipe path the regeneration of the BHK page (fresh 3-source TRNG words into page 126 + TAMP BKP reload) — Trezor's `secret_safety_erase` — so the SE050 SCP03/admin credentials are dead instantly even if the SE delete never runs; then erase page-124/123/127 and run both SE factory resets. (2) Replace plain-bool wipe verdicts with `fi::CfiCounter`-style sentinels with FI-double reads, and treat 'unknown' as 'not wiped' (never coerce). (3) At boot, if the page-125 flag is armed, re-assert: pages 123–127 blank (except flag), OPTIGA F1E1/F1D1 absent via check_exists through the shield, SE050 ENTROPY/USERID absent via CheckObjectExists — only then clear the flag; otherwise resume the wipe. (4) Include the duress object set (F1D8/E121, DURESS_*) in the wipe list so decoys do not survive. (5) Record one receipt line in the journal so a forensic read shows 'wiped at boot N'.
rationale: Ledger's 1.4 fix made the user-zone wipe 'verified at startup'; Trezor's BHK regeneration gives a single atomic action that invalidates every BHK-wrapped secret regardless of what happens afterwards. pq1 already owns the BHK axis for SE050 (owner decision 2026-09-21) so the BHK-first step costs one page program and immediately strengthens the 10-wrong-PIN brick and the tamp-wipe path against power-cut and glitch interruption.
repo_evidence: secure/src/hw/flash.rs:626-691 wipe flag: ADMIN_PAGE_ADDR+16, covers the SE050 admin object only
secure/src/se050/mod.rs:3168-3238 Se050::factory_reset_admin; secure/src/dual_se.rs:631-648 factory_reset_admin — no BHK regeneration step
secure/src/nsc/cmd_request_unlock.rs:190-211 trigger_lockout_wipe — sequential, no boot-time verification contract
secure/src/hw/bhk.rs:318-421 load_and_lock exists; no 'regenerate' wipe primitive
Issues #106 (SE17-3 verdict coercion), #123 (OP17-8 atomicity), #107 (duress objects survive wipes), #129, #168 (F23), #47
vendor_precedent: Trezor core/embed/sec/secret/stm32u5/secret.c:393-442,655-658 (secret_safety_erase regenerates BHK → all BHK-wrapped storage invalid); Ledger firmware 1.4 'wipe verified at startup' (LSB-003 fix); Trezor storage.c:1163-1303 (wipe when any counter says so, verified increments).
risks: BHK-first wipe interacts with the #712/#204 recoverability bug (a regenerated BHK is exactly the 'SE050 unreachable' state) — acceptable here because the goal IS unrecoverability, but the re-pair/OID-range-bump story for the next wallet (#168) must be designed alongside; boot-time resume must be idempotent under repeated power cuts; wipe decisions must still never be driven by an unauthenticated SW (SE-03).
